newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES CLOSE DOWN 3.0 PCT ON LUJIAZUI.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES CLOSE DOWN 3.0 PCT ON LUJIAZUI.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended down nearly three percent on Monday, dragged lower by selling of property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co, brokers said.
The property firm fell $0.132 to its 10 percent limit down to end at $1.188 after announcing a plunge in 1997 interim profits on Friday.
The B index closed down 2.213 points or 2.95 percent to 72.710 on turnover of $10.067 million, compared with $11.614 million in the previous session.
Lujiazui, which has a heavy weighting in the Shanghai B share index, posted net profits of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, down 67 percent from the first half of 1996.
The company, which develops property in Shanghai's Pudong development zone, blamed the poor showing on losses by a subsidiary.
"Selling in Lujiazui after it posted poor interim results pushed the index down sharply," said a broker at a major domestic securities firm.
"Lujiazui could fall further, which may hurt market sentiment even more," he said.
Although analysts had widely predicted weak interim results for Lujiazui due to oversupply in the Shanghai property market, the sharpness of the fall caught some investors by surprise, brokers said.
The company was suspended from trading for the morning session for the results announcement and resumed trading in the afternoon, quickly falling to its limit down, they said.
Lujiazui was the biggest loser on Monday. Another developer with ties to Shanghai's Pudong, Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co, fell $0.030 or 5.88 percent to $0.480.
